claim: A check's processor ceiling is charged the cost of building the shadow the change leaves, which is one cost every check at that landing shares. The check that trips is whichever asks the index first, and the number in the refusal is that shared settle rather than the check's own work. So a landing is refused by a check whose own reading is a hundredth of what it was charged for, raising that check's ceiling buys a landing rather than a class, and the next big change refuses under a different check's name.

evidence:
Measured on 2026-09-15. `introduced-property-is-a-part` refused three landings at 11.357, 11.397 and 11.165 processor seconds against the 10 its page states — twice over the `design-interfaces` rename at 2332 and 3479 edits, once more after. The number barely moved between a 2332-edit change and a 3479-edit one, which is what first made me look past the change's size.

What the check itself costs. Over a plain shadow of this repository, `everyType` answers all 480 page types in 0.04 processor seconds, `sourceOf` in 0.00, and `refusalsOver` in 0.05 — nine hundredths of a second in total, against a ceiling of ten seconds.

Where the time is. Over a change of 1000 paths of which 500 are moves, `shadowFor` takes 1.32 processor seconds to build, and the same three pieces of the check then take 0.00, 0.00 and 0.12. So at that size the settle is eleven times the check, and the real change was three and a half times that size again.

Why it lands on this check. `pageOf` is memoized on the shadow and `shadow.index` is lazy, so the settle is paid once per landing, by whichever check first asks the index for anything. `introduced-property-is-a-part` asks `pageTypesIn` in its first line. It is not slow; it is early.

What I ruled out on the way, since each was a reading I held and had to give up. Not the page-type reads: 480 of them cost 0.04 processor seconds through `pageOf` and 0.00 through `pageByPath`, on a plain shadow and under an overlay alike. Not the gathering of properties over the types a page type extends: memoizing the page-type slug lookup in `declared-properties`, landed as `275358b5026`, moved the refusal by 0.2 seconds, which is the measurement that should have told me the gathering was never the cost.

What a raise would buy. The refusal names one check, so a raise is written on one check's page. The settle keeps growing with the change, and the next landing large enough to pass ten seconds of settle refuses under whichever check happens to ask first — a name that says nothing about what was slow.

The condition a mend would meet: what a check is charged is what that check did, so a cost every check at a landing shares is either paid before the checks or charged to the landing rather than to one check's page.
